prompt: Company profile: Grocery distribution center in Tolleson, Arizona; 300 employees. Situation: The company is converting its forklift fleet from propane to electric and building a battery charging/changing area: 40 chargers, a battery-washing station, and lead-acid batteries containing sulfuric acid electrolyte. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
**Compliance Obligations Register – Tolleson Distribution Center Electric Forklift Conversion**

---

### **1. Hazardous Waste Management – Spent Lead-Acid Batteries & Sulfuric Acid Waste**
- **Requirement**: Classify, store, manifest, and dispose of spent lead-acid batteries, waste sulfuric acid, and lead-contaminated wash water as hazardous waste per RCRA Subtitle C. Maintain 3-year manifests, use licensed transporters, and store batteries on sealed containment pallets with secondary containment.
- **Source**: Arizona Revised Statutes §49-922; 40 CFR 262 (EPA RCRA); ADEQ R18-8-260 (Hazardous Waste Management)
- **Applicability**: 40 batteries contain ~1,200 lbs of lead and 400 gallons of sulfuric acid. Battery washing station generates lead/acid-contaminated wastewater. Facility becomes a hazardous waste generator.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Monthly inspection of waste storage area (check containment, labeling, accumulation dates); quarterly review of waste manifests for accuracy; annual third-party waste audit; ADEQ inspection every 1-3 years based on generator status. Records: inspection logs, manifest copies, audit reports.

---

### **2. Industrial Wastewater Discharge Permit & pH Pretreatment**
- **Requirement**: Obtain Industrial Wastewater Discharge Permit from Tolleson City or Maricopa County prior to operating battery wash station. Continuously monitor and maintain discharge pH between 6-9 SU. Pretreat to remove lead (<0.05 mg/L) and sulfates before discharge to POTW.
- **Source**: Tolleson Municipal Code §13-4 (Sewer Use); Maricopa County Environmental Services Dept. Rules; Arizona Administrative Code R18-9-A201
- **Applicability**: Battery wash station effluent contains sulfuric acid (pH <2) and dissolved lead. Direct discharge violates local sewer ordinances and Arizona Aquifer Protection rules.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Daily pH meter calibration check; weekly composite sampling with lab analysis (pH, lead, sulfates); monthly discharge report to municipality; annual permit renewal. Records: lab results, calibration logs, discharge reports.

---

### **3. Air Quality – Hydrogen Gas Ventilation & Explosion Prevention**
- **Requirement**: Install mechanical ventilation maintaining hydrogen concentration <25% of LEL (1% by volume) in charging area. Provide hydrogen gas detectors with audible alarms at 0.4% H₂. Maintain 3-foot clearance around chargers. Prohibit ignition sources.
- **Source**: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(g); NFPA 2 Hydrogen Technologies Code; Maricopa County Air Quality Dept. Rule 310 (Fugitive Emissions)
- **Applicability**: 40 chargers simultaneously charging lead-acid batteries generate explosive hydrogen gas. Tolleson is in Maricopa County non-attainment area.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 45001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Quarterly air sampling for hydrogen concentration; monthly functional test of ventilation fans and gas detectors; annual calibration of H₂ sensors by certified technician; daily visual clearance checks. Records: air sampling reports, maintenance logs, alarm test records.

---

### **4. Hazard Communication (HazCom) Program for Sulfuric Acid & Lead**
- **Requirement**: Maintain current Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for sulfuric acid electrolyte and lead compounds. Train all affected 300 employees on chemical hazards, PPE, emergency procedures before assignment and annually. Label all battery stations, wash area, and storage with HCS pictograms.
- **Source**: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 (Hazard Communication Standard); Arizona Division of Occupational Safety & Health (ADOSH) adopts federal standard
- **Applicability**: All warehouse employees, maintenance staff, and battery room workers handle or work near batteries containing corrosive sulfuric acid and toxic lead.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 45001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Annual training documentation audit; monthly SDS binder audit; quarterly workplace labeling inspection; post-training competency assessment. Records: training sign-in sheets, quiz results, SDS inventory, inspection checklists.

---

### **5. Personal Protective Equipment – Acid-Resistant Gear**
- **Requirement**: Provide and enforce use of: acid-resistant gloves (neoprene, minimum 14 mil), face shields (ANSI Z87.1), chemical splash goggles, acid-resistant aprons, and steel-toe boots for all battery handling, charging, and washing tasks. Conduct annual hazard assessment.
- **Source**: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.132 (PPE General Requirements); 1910.133 (Eye/Face); 1910.138 (Hand Protection)
- **Applicability**: 40 daily battery changes and wash operations create high potential for sulfuric acid splashes and lead dust exposure.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 45001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Monthly PPE condition inspections; quarterly observational audits of PPE usage; annual hazard assessment review; incident investigation for any acid exposure. Records: PPE issue logs, inspection records, audit findings.

---

### **6. Emergency Eyewash & Safety Shower – ANSI Z358.1**
- **Requirement**: Install emergency eyewash and shower units within 10 seconds (55 feet) unobstructed travel distance of battery charging/washing stations. Provide tepid water (60-100°F). Activate/test weekly for 3 minutes. Annual full ANSI compliance inspection.
- **Source**: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.151(c); ANSI Z358.1-2014 Emergency Eyewash and Shower Equipment
- **Applicability**: Sulfuric acid exposure requires immediate 15-minute flushing to prevent permanent injury. 300 employees must have access.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 45001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Weekly activation test (document water flow, clarity, temperature); annual third-party ANSI inspection; post-incident functional verification. Records: test logs, inspection certificates, maintenance work orders.

---

### **7. Battery Charging Area Electrical Safety & LOTO**
- **Requirement**: Install 40 chargers per NEC Article 625 (Electric Vehicle Charging). Provide GFCI protection, lockable disconnects, and dedicated circuits. Develop LOTO procedures for charger maintenance. Inspect cords monthly.
- **Source**: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.305; NFPA 70 National Electrical Code; 29 CFR 1910.147 (LOTO)
- **Applicability**: High-voltage charging equipment (208/240V) in wet/corrosive environment creates shock and arc-flash hazards.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 45001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Monthly visual electrical inspection; annual LOTO audit and procedure review; quarterly energized work permit review; annual thermographic scan of electrical panels. Records: inspection tags, LOTO logs, audit reports.

---

### **8. Fire Safety & Suppression in Charging Area**
- **Requirement**: Install Class C fire extinguishers (CO₂ or dry chemical) within 30 feet. Provide smoke/heat detection tied to building fire alarm. Maintain 3-foot charger clearance. Comply with Tolleson Fire Marshal requirements for new construction permit.
- **Source**: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.157; NFPA 1 Fire Code; Tolleson Fire Dept. Code Enforcement
- **Applicability**: Hydrogen gas and electrical equipment create fire/explosion risk. 300-employee facility requires robust emergency response.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 45001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Monthly fire extinguisher pressure checks; annual fire system certification; quarterly fire drill including battery area scenario; daily clearance inspections. Records: extinguisher tags, inspection certificates, drill reports.

---

### **9. Stormwater Pollution Prevention – AZPDES**
- **Requirement**: If battery storage/charging area is exposed to rain, obtain AZPDES Multi-Sector General Permit (MSGP) and develop Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP). Maintain secondary containment, conduct quarterly stormwater sampling for pH and lead.
- **Source**: Arizona Department of Environmental Quality AZPDES Program; 40 CFR 122 (EPA NPDES)
- **Applicability**: Tolleson monsoon season (July-Sept) could cause acid/lead runoff from outdoor battery storage or wash area. Facility >1 acre requires permit.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Quarterly stormwater visual inspections; semi-annual lab sampling (pH, lead); annual SWPPP review; post-rainfall event inspections. Records: inspection forms, lab reports, SWPPP updates.

---

### **10. Medical Surveillance for Lead Exposure**
- **Requirement**: If air monitoring shows lead exposure >30 µg/m³ (8-hour TWA), implement medical surveillance including baseline and bi-annual blood lead testing (BLL) for exposed employees. Remove employees if BLL >60 µg/dL.
- **Source**: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1025 (Lead Standard); Arizona ADOSH adopts federal standard
- **Applicability**: Battery changing and washing can aerosolize lead compounds. 300 employees with potential exposure.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 45001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Initial air monitoring within 30 days of operation; annual exposure reassessment; bi-annual blood lead tests for 20+ exposed employees; annual medical surveillance program review. Records: air sampling data, BLL results, medical removal logs.

---

### **11. Battery Storage & Handling – Secondary Containment**
- **Requirement**: Store all lead-acid batteries on sealed containment pallets with 110% secondary containment capacity. Segregate from incompatible materials. Ensure storage area ventilation prevents hydrogen accumulation.
- **Source**: EPA RCRA 40 CFR 265.173 (Container Requirements); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(g)
- **Applicability**: 40+ batteries in storage contain ~400 gallons of sulfuric acid. Spill potential during storage.
- **ISO Clause**: Both ISO 14001 6.1.3 and ISO 45001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Weekly visual inspection of containment integrity; monthly measurement of containment liquid levels; annual third-party spill response readiness audit. Records: inspection checklist, spill kit inventory, audit report.

---

### **12. Building & Electrical Permits for Charging Infrastructure**
- **Requirement**: Obtain Tolleson building permit, electrical permit, and fire department plan review for new 40-charger installation. Comply with IBC, NEC, and local amendments. Final inspection before operation.
- **Source**: Tolleson Municipal Code Ch. 3 (Buildings); International Building Code (IBC) 2018; NFPA 70 NEC 2020
- **Applicability**: New construction of dedicated charging area with significant electrical load (estimated 800+ amps) requires permitting.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 45001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Pre-construction plan submission; inspections at 25%, 50%, 100% completion; final certificate of occupancy; annual building safety inspection. Records: permits, inspection sign-offs, COO.

---

### **13. Recordkeeping Retention Requirements**
- **Requirement**: Maintain training records for 3 years, medical surveillance records for duration of employment +30 years, waste manifests for 3 years, inspection logs for 5 years, and incident reports for 5 years.
- **Source**: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1025 (Lead); 1910.1200 (HazCom); ADEQ R18-8-270; ISO 14001/45001 7.5
- **Applicability**: All battery-related activities generate records subject to regulatory retention.
- **ISO Clause**: Both ISO 14001 6.1.3 and ISO 45001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Quarterly internal audit of record completeness; annual legal compliance review of retention schedule; secure offsite backup verification. Records: audit reports, retention schedule, archive logs.

---

### **14. DOT Hazardous Materials Shipping**
- **Requirement**: If shipping >1,000 lbs of spent batteries offsite, comply with DOT hazmat shipping: proper UN2794 labeling, employee training, shipping papers, emergency response info. Use licensed hauler.
- **Source**: 49 CFR 172 (DOT Hazardous Materials Regulations)
- **Applicability**: Disposal of 40 spent batteries (~2,000 lbs) triggers DOT hazmat requirements.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Review of transporter DOT credentials annually; pre-shipment documentation check; annual employee hazmat training if shipping directly. Records: transporter licenses, shipping papers, training certs.

---

### **15. Energy Management & Greenhouse Gas Reporting**
- **Requirement**: If total facility electricity usage exceeds 10,000 MWh/year, report GHG emissions to EPA under 40 CFR 98. Calculate and report Scope 1 (propane reduction) and Scope 2 (electricity increase) emissions.
- **Source**: 40 CFR 98 (EPA GHG Reporting); Arizona Corporation Commission energy efficiency programs
- **Applicability**: 40 chargers (15 kW each) operating 16 hrs/day = 3,504 MWh/year + facility baseline may exceed threshold. Propane reduction offsets must be tracked.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001 6.1.3
- **Compliance Evaluation (9.1.2)**: Monthly electricity metering; annual GHG emissions calculation; March 31 annual reporting deadline to EPA; quarterly energy performance review. Records: utility bills, GHG reports, emission factors.

---

**Summary Evaluation Framework (ISO 9.1.2):**
- **How**: Combination of internal audits, regulatory inspections, third-party assessments, continuous monitoring (pH, hydrogen), and documentation reviews.
- **When**: Daily (visual checks), weekly (testing), monthly (inspections/sampling), quarterly (audits/sampling), annually (comprehensive reviews, permit renewals, training).
- **Responsibility**: EHS Manager maintains register, conducts audits; Facility Manager oversees daily checks; HR maintains training/medical records; Maintenance performs equipment tests.
- **Records**: All evaluations documented in centralized EHS management system with automated reminders for critical deadlines (permit renewals, annual audits).
